tasks.short: Schedule sessions with couples and families, counsel clients on relationships, separation, child rearing and money, and write session notes.

steps.what: Couple or family books a session in the client portal from the therapist's open slots
Family therapist schedules sessions with couples and families by phone and e-mail today; after the change, confirms portal bookings and reschedules by phone when needed
Family therapist counsels clients on unsatisfactory relationships, divorce, child rearing or financial difficulties
Family therapist writes session notes

tasks.design: Couples and families book sessions in the client portal from the therapist's open slots, so dates are not agreed by phone and e-mail with several people. After each session, the therapist speaks a short summary and speech-driven reporting drafts the note; a validator flags risk statements not in the summary, and the therapist approves before saving. Counselling stays with the therapist; sessions are not recorded.
tasks.previous_blocker: Dates were agreed with several family members by phone and notes typed after sessions.
tasks.enabler_now: Speech-driven reporting is used in mental health care; client portals offer booking.
tasks.still_hard: Drafts can add statements the therapist did not make.
tasks.human_edge: Staying neutral between two partners in conflict.
tasks.altitude: The therapist corrects drafts instead of typing.

evidence.claim: Attendi turns spoken notes into a SOEP report or letter in the care record; 300+ care organisations use it.
UK social workers found invented suicidal ideation in AI-drafted notes.
Recording staff conversations needs works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the client request to session notes; referral is outside.
Input contract: goals in the record; fallback is typing notes.
Families book online (s0) in about the time calls took; their time is outside the therapist's savings and is not counted again as new work.
s3 is part of keeping progress notes in case files, which sibling task 21-1013.00:9187 covers; its saving is counted there, so s3 keeps its full time here.
research_questions: How often does the validator flag a risk statement?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: about half of families keep phoning to agree dates, so s1 keeps 70 (2.2); high: most families book in the portal (4.9).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read the referral and intake information, hold the intake talk, decide whether to counsel or refer, write the referral letter, check it, and send it.

steps.what: Client fills a short intake questionnaire online before the first talk
Family therapist reads the referral and intake information
Family therapist holds the intake talk with the client
Family therapist determines whether clients should be counseled or referred to other specialists
Family therapist writes the referral letter
Family therapist checks the final referral letter
Family therapist sends the checked referral to the specialist through the secure care exchange

tasks.design: Referrals arrive in the record ({OTHER}) through the secure care exchange, and clients fill a short intake questionnaire online before the first talk, so the therapist does not gather this by hand. The referral letter template fills client details and the reason from the intake. Once the therapist has checked the letter, it goes to the specialist through the secure exchange. Deciding to counsel or refer stays with the therapist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Referral information came on paper and letters were typed from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Secure care exchanges and online intake questionnaires are common.
tasks.still_hard: Waiting lists at specialists are long.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a couple's conflict hides a psychiatric problem that needs another specialist.

evidence.claim: Secure care exchanges and online intake questionnaires can bring referral data into the record.
Health data are special category data under GDPR article 9.

assumptions: Boundary: from the referral to the referral sent; the specialist's treatment is outside.
Input contract: referrers use the secure exchange; fallback is paper.

Clients spend a little time on the online questionnaire (s0); priced as customer time and not counted again as new work. s4 keeps 70 because the therapist writes the reason and the question for the specialist; the template fills client details. s6 keeps 10 for the send itself.

incremental.description: No new work: reading the intake questionnaire is part of s1, and the client's time is shown in s0.

approvals.approved_version: The referral letter with client details and the reason for referral exactly as checked by the therapist in s5, sent once through the secure care exchange to the named specialist; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many referrers keep sending paper and clients skip the questionnaire, so s1 keeps 85, and letters are mostly written by hand, so s4 keeps 85 (8.9); high: exchange and template as designed (15.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Hold supervision sessions, review supervisees' case notes, plan supervision and caseloads, and record supervision.

steps.what: Family therapist supervises other counselors and social service staff in sessions
Family therapist reviews supervisees' case notes
Family therapist plans supervision and caseloads in a spreadsheet
Family therapist records the supervision

tasks.design: A caseload view in the case system ({OTHER}) shows each supervisee's open cases, last contact and overdue reviews, so the therapist opens only the cases that need discussion and does not keep a separate spreadsheet. Supervision is recorded in a short template. Supervising staff stays with the therapist; the view is not used to rate staff without works council consent.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cases were found by paging through records and caseloads kept in spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Case systems can show caseload views per worker.
tasks.still_hard: Caseload numbers say little about case difficulty.
tasks.human_edge: Helping a young counsellor through a case that affects them personally.

evidence.claim: Case systems can show caseload views with last contact and overdue reviews.
Systems able to monitor staff performance need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from supervision due to supervision recorded; appraisal is outside.
Input contract: case data current; fallback is paging through records.

Supervision sessions do not change. s3 keeps 65 because deciding caseloads stays; the view removes keeping a separate spreadsheet. s4 keeps 85 because the therapist writes what was discussed and agreed; the template lists the cases from the view.
Works council consent comes before the caseload view.

incremental.description: Family therapist checks caseload data with supervisees.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: case data are often not current, so the therapist still pages through records (s2 keeps 85) and checks caseloads by hand (s3 keeps 80) (7.0); high: a current caseload view (12.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Arrange case consultations, prepare the case summary, confer with counsellors, doctors and other professionals, and record agreements.

steps.what: Family therapist arranges case consultations by e-mail and phone
Family therapist asks and records the client's consent to share the case summary with the partners
Family therapist prepares the case summary
Family therapist checks the final case summary: facts against the record, only what the consent covers, and the partners it goes to
Family therapist shares the checked case summary and request with the consultation partners
Family therapist confers with other counselors, doctors and professionals to analyze individual cases
Family therapist records the agreements

tasks.design: Recurring consultation slots with the regular partners sit in a shared agenda ({CALENDAR}), with a short request form per case, so consultations are not arranged case by case by e-mail. The case summary template fills goals and progress from the record ({OTHER}), shared only with the client's consent. The therapist checks each summary before it is shared. Agreements are written in the record as today, a first record that keeps its time. Conferring stays with the therapist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Consultations were arranged by e-mail and summaries written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared agendas and record templates fill summaries from existing data.
tasks.human_edge: Agreeing who leads when a family sees four professionals.

reach.learn: Whether agreements are clear to everyone.

evidence.claim: Record templates can fill case summaries from goals and progress already recorded.
Health data are special category data under GDPR article 9.

assumptions: Boundary: from the case question to agreements recorded; carrying out the agreements is outside.
Input contract: client consent for sharing; fallback is an anonymised summary.

Conferring, recording agreements and checking summaries before they are shared do not change. s2 keeps 60 because the template fills goals and progress from the record and the therapist writes the case question.

incremental.description: No new work: recording consent is shown as step s1b.

approvals.approved_version: The case summary and request exactly as checked by the therapist in s2b, within the client's recorded consent, shared once with the named consultation partners; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many partners do not use the shared slots, so s1 keeps 70 (10.8); high: recurring slots as designed (16.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The family therapist keeps counselling, deciding on referrals, supervising and conferring; phone scheduling, typed notes and spreadsheets shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A therapist with more time for families.
